source_revision: not-reviewed: provider terms not read; automation surface per docs/research/headless-ai-coding-controller-verified-2026-10-12.md (R2, 2026-10-12)
notes: Automation surface: `claude -p` with structured output, resume and `claude auth status`, per R2 sections 'Verified provider adapter design' (adapter matrix) and 'Compliance and authentication boundary'; TDD 4.1. Version: 2.1.296 is what `claude --version` reported on the development host on 2026-10-12 (version flag only; no prompt run, no conformance suite yet). Assumption: the range >=2.1.296 <2.2.0 (same minor series) is a Proposed conservative bound, not a provider statement; R2 gives no version numbers. Credentials: Switchboard never reads, copies, logs or exports Claude Code credentials, never starts login and never scrapes dashboards or reimplements the network protocol; it asks the native CLI for status and returns AUTH_REQUIRED naming the native login (ADR-0003, FR-AUTH-02). Terms: this manifest records that the CLI documents headless use (technical evidence only); it makes no claim that any use complies with Anthropic's terms. Commercial, resale, multi-user or credential-sharing use requires a per-provider policy review first (NFR-COMP-01). Review date: 2026-10-12 (Delegated agent review, not owner-approved). Git writes (FR-GIT-01, T2.2): verified against `claude --help` 2.1.296 text only (no prompt run). Documented controls used: `--disallowedTools <tools...>` (help: "Comma or space-separated list of tool names to deny (e.g. \"Bash(git *) Edit\")") carries deny rules `Bash(git <verb>)` and `Bash(git <verb> *)` for commit, ref-changing and push subcommands, git global options (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree) and `gh`; `--restricted` (help: "lets only a person or the configured permission handler approve writes to settings, git and tool-configuration files") with `--permission-prompts none`; and no Bash tool unless the operator allowlists exact commands, where any entry that could write Git makes the run Ineligible. Assumptions: `*` matches any suffix, deny wins over allow, and deny rules for a tool absent from --tools are accepted. Limits: the rules are lexical (no aliases, scripts run by an allowlisted build tool, or absolute paths to git). Commit and attribution: the help documents no flag that disables Claude Code's own commit or attribution behaviour except `--bare` ("skip ... attribution"), which forces API-key auth and is not used (ADR-0015); settings files are never written (FR-POL-08). Remaining controls: FR-GIT-03 (M9) and FR-GIT-06. Live behaviour unverified (live smoke check C-G2). Native controls (T3.0, 2026-10-13, TDD 4.1.1; Delegated): the installed `claude --help` 2.1.296 (read only, no prompt run) lists no sandbox option and no network option; "sandboxes" appears only in the advice on `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`, so no per-run native sandbox exists without `--settings` or global configuration, and a settings-based one is Unknown until the live check T3.9 (R-10; `--settings` is also barred by ADR-0015). Compile matrix (T3.5, 2026-10-13; Delegated, Proposed, argv tests only, no prompt run): inspect-untrusted and edit-untrusted compile as in M2; trusted-development compiles with the same flags as edit-untrusted (--safe-mode --restricted --strict-mcp-config, dontAsk, --permission-prompts none, explicit --tools/--allowedTools, the Git --disallowedTools deny rules) when its network is off, its shell is none or an exact allowlist, and its repository configuration is disabled; network allowlist or policy, shell broad (Q-34) and repository configuration approved-only or allowlisted are Ineligible: CAPABILITY_MISSING (no documented control); test-sandboxed stays Ineligible: PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED (FR-POL-06, R-10, Q-16) until T3.9 or T3.1; Privileged (T3.5, T3.17, 2026-10-13; Delegated, Proposed, argv tests only, no prompt run): compiled from the approved scope. Network must be `on` (WebFetch named in --tools); network off or allowlist, repository configuration approved or enabled, read-only files with broad shell, and an exact shell allowlist under bypass are Ineligible: CAPABILITY_MISSING. bypass false: the trusted-development flags with Bash (exact rules or the allow rule `Bash` for broad). bypass true: only when CompileRequest.bypassApproved is true (else Ineligible: PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED), the help-documented `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (help: "Bypass all permission checks. Recommended only for sandboxes with no internet access.") replaces `--permission-mode dontAsk`, `--restricted` is omitted (help: it "refuses bypassPermissions"; owner decision 19, answers Q-33 for the compile), and --safe-mode, --strict-mcp-config, --permission-prompts none, --tools and the Git --disallowedTools deny rules are kept; no --add-dir or --worktree. Assumptions, unverified (R-26, live check T3.9): that deny rules and --tools still apply under --dangerously-skip-permissions, and that omitting --permission-mode is right (the help does not say how the two combine). The argv audit admits the flag only for privileged, bypassApproved and scope bypass (T3.17). Network off holds at the tool level only, so an allowlisted command is not network-confined (R-36, Q-34). Linux only; macOS (NFR-PORT-02) and Windows (NFR-PORT-03) are not supported yet. T9.0 spike (2026-10-13; Delegated; installed `claude --help`, `claude mcp --help` and `claude mcp add --help` 2.1.296 read only, no prompt run, no login, no `mcp list`/`mcp add`; Git 2.43.0 for the Git findings; TDD 3.10, LLD 12): Per-run MCP definition: `--mcp-config <configs...>` (help: "Load MCP servers from JSON files or strings (space-separated)") with `--strict-mcp-config` (help: "Only use MCP servers from --mcp-config, ignoring all other MCP configurations"); `claude mcp add`/`add-json` write local, user or project configuration and are not used (FR-POL-08). Unverified, live check needed: the top-level JSON shape of `--mcp-config` (add-json documents only stdio, SSE, HTTP, WebSocket servers); the allow-rule form of an MCP tool; whether an MCP tool call prompts, and so is denied, under dontAsk with --permission-prompts none unless pre-allowed; whether --safe-mode also disables a server given by --mcp-config. Until answered this adapter must not declare an injected commit channel. ADR-0015 and the argv audit currently bar `--mcp-config` entirely; the channel needs it, so narrowing that bar to the controller-generated shim definition is a proposed ADR (ROADMAP Q-40), not applied here, and no compile code changed. Sandbox and socket: the help lists no sandbox option, so these flags apply none; whether the shim can reach a Unix socket is Unknown: live check. Deny-rule syntax: the only documented form is the help example `\"Bash(git *) Edit\"`; matching semantics stay an Assumption. Gaps in the emitted rules, verified on Git 2.43.0 as Git behaviour (Claude's matcher not run): Git global options placed before the subcommand are not denied except -C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, and `git --no-pager commit`, `git -P commit` and `git --no-optional-locks commit` all created commits in a test repository, so a purely lexical `Bash(git commit *)` rule does not see them (ROADMAP R-43); also not covered are --config-env, --exec-path, --namespace, --bare, an absolute path to git, `git-<name>` programs, and ref-affecting subcommands missing from GIT_WRITE_SUBCOMMANDS (reflog, pack-refs, gc, prune, maintenance; `git pack-refs --all` and `git reflog expire` ran in the test repository). Commit and attribution: no setting beyond `--bare` (\"skip ... attribution\") appears in the help, `--bare` is unusable (ADR-0015); the FR-GIT-04 sanitiser stays necessary and no provider attribution setting is relied on. Result: T9.0 is Partial for Claude Code (ROADMAP 6.3). T9.4b (2026-10-13; Delegated; ADR-0029; argv tests and a replay script only, no prompt run): behind the operator opt-in providers.claude-code.git_channel (default false, UNSUPPORTED until the ADR-0029 live checks pass) the adapter declares an injected channel and appends `--mcp-config <run channel dir>/mcp-config.json --allowedTools mcp__switchboard-git__commit[ mcp__switchboard-git__push]`; the 0600 file holds one stdio server and an env reference, never the token; the argv audit admits only that shape. Without the opt-in nothing changes.
